folgava: folgar — he was resting, taking his ease (imperfect 3rd sg.; = holgaba; modern holgar 'to rest, be idle')
âquel: a + aquel — to that (preposition a + demonstrative aquel, run together; Pidal prints â with a circumflex and gives no note; âquel rey 'to that king', the one the news came to; = a aquel)
sevilla: Sevilla — Seville; from 1091 held by the Almoravids, so rey de Sevilla is the Almoravid general who governed it (Pidal's note to v. 1222; = Sevilla)
enparan: enparar — they defend, protect (present 3rd pl.; non gela enparan 'they do not hold it against him', i.e. the Moors no longer defend Valencia against the Çid; whose 'him' is meant is uncertain; = amparan)
aprés: aprés — near, close by (preposition, with de; aprés de la uerta 'close by the orchard-land'; no modern form, = cerca de, junto a)
uerta: uerta — irrigated orchard-land, here the plain round Valencia (= huerta, spelled without h)
arrancólos: arrancar + los — he routed them (preterite 3rd sg. arrancó + enclitic los; = los arrancó, 'los derrotó, los hizo huir')
luenga: luengo — long (fem. sg., Latin longus; la luenga barba 'the long beard'; modern luengo survives only archaically, = larga)
xúcar: Xúcar — the river Júcar, south of Valencia (= Júcar; x = sh-sound)
veriédes: veer — you would see (conditional 2nd pl., old -iédes ending; = veríais; the minstrel's aside to the audience)
barata: barata — apparently 'turmoil, confusion, a scramble' (i veriédes barata 'there you would have seen a scramble'); the word otherwise means a dealing, a bargain; no note in Pidal; sense uncertain
arruenço: arruenço — (en arruenço) drifting, floundering; Pidal glosses the line 'los moros ronceando (a la ronza contra la corriente) bebían agua sin querer', 'the Moors, drifting against the current, drank water unwillingly'; Pidal restores the first r; no modern form; exact sense uncertain
escapa: escapar — he escapes, gets away (present 3rd sg.; = escapa)
provechosa: provechoso — profitable, advantageous (fem. sg.; mas mucho fue provechosa 'was more profitable'; = provechosa)
menores: menor — lesser (masc. pl.; los menores 'the lesser men', apparently the rank and file; no note in Pidal; = menores)
cayeron: caer — they fell (preterite 3rd pl.; cayeron çient marcos 'a hundred marks fell to them', i.e. came to each one's share; = cayeron)
allongando: allongar — lengthening, growing longer (gerund; = alongando; modern alongar is rare, closest alargando, alargar)
dixera: dezir — he had said (-ra form in its old pluperfect sense, 3rd sg.; ca dixera 'for he had said'; = había dicho, modern dijera)
atanto: atanto — to such a degree, so, thus (a + tanto; de la su boca atanto 'from his own mouth, just so', introducing the oath; sense inferred, no note in Pidal; modern tanto)
alffonsso: Alffonsso — Alfonso VI, king of León and Castile who exiled the Cid (= Alfonso)
entrarié: entrar — it would enter (conditional 3rd sg., -ié ending; nin entrarié en ella tigera 'nor would shears touch it'; = entraría)
tigera: tigera — scissors, shears (fem. sg., Latin tonsoria; = tijera, modern normally pl. tijeras)
tajado: tajar — cut (past part. masc. sg.; avrié tajado 'he would have cut'; = tajado, closest cortado; modern tajar 'to slice')
fablassen: fablar — they should speak, might speak (imperfect subjunctive 3rd pl., e que fablassen desto 'and that they should talk of it'; = hablasen)
folgando: folgar — resting, taking ease (gerund; está folgando 'is resting'; = holgando)
exieron: exir — they went out, left (preterite 3rd pl.; = salieron; no modern exir)
ritad: ritad — uncertain: no note in Pidal; most likely a noun made on rico, 'riches, wealth' (de ritad son abondados 'they are abounding in wealth'), like rictad (v. 688, Pidal 'riqueza') and rritad (v. 1189); = riqueza (if so)
abondados: abondar — provided, enriched, supplied in abundance (past part. masc. pl., with son; = abastecidos, abundantes; modern abundar 'to abound')
provando: provar — trying, putting to the test, experiencing (gerund; ivan provando 'were coming to experience'; = probando)
veelo: veer + lo — he sees it (present 3rd sg. vee + enclitic lo; veelo mio Çid que … 'the Cid sees it, that …'; = lo ve)
tomados: tomar — taken (past part. masc. pl., agreeing with averes; los averes que avién tomados 'the goods they had taken'; = tomados)
sis: si + se — if … themselves (conjunction si + reflexive se; que sis pudiessen ir 'that if they could go away'; = si se)
pudiessen: poder — they could, were able (imperfect subjunctive 3rd pl.; = pudiesen)
conssejado: consejar — advised, counselled (past part. masc. sg.; Minaya lo ovo conssejado 'Minaya had advised it'; = aconsejado)
ningún: ninguno — no, any (apocopated masc. sg. before a noun; ningún omne 'no man'; = ningún)
spidiés: espedir(se) — (that) he should take leave (imperfect subjunctive 3rd sg., espidiesse with its final -e lost (-sse > -s) and its e- dropped; ques le non spidiés = que + se + le + non + spidiés 'who should not take leave of him'; = se despidiese, despedirse)
besás: besar — (that) he should kiss (imperfect subjunctive 3rd sg., besasse with -se lost; o nol besás la mano 'or kiss not his hand', the formal leave-taking; = besase)
sil: si + le — if … him (si + enclitic le; sil pudiessen prender 'if they could seize him'; = si le)
alcançado: alcançar — overtaken, caught (past part. masc. sg.; o fosse alcançado 'or were overtaken'; = alcanzado)
tomássenle: tomar + le — let them take from him (imperfect subjunctive 3rd pl. tomassen + enclitic le, dative 'from him', dependent on mandó que; = le tomasen)
pusiéssenle: poner + le — let them put him (imperfect subjunctive 3rd pl. pusiessen + enclitic le as direct object, leísmo; = lo pusiesen)
palo: palo — stake, pole, here the gallows-post (Pidal: 'horca'; = palo)
saber: saber — to know, to find out (infinitive; quiero saber recabdo 'I want to learn the account'; = saber)
meterlos: meter + los + he — I shall put them (split future: infinitive meter + enclitic los + he, 1st sg.; = los meteré)
escripto: escripto — writing, written record (noun; en escripto 'in writing', i.e. on a list; Latin scriptum; = escrito)
sean: seer — let them be (present subjunctive 3rd pl., jussive; todos sean contados 'let them all be counted'; = sean)
furtare: furtar — (if) he steal (future subjunctive 3rd sg., with algunos; with no object, apparently 'steal away, slip off', though 'steal' outright is possible; no note in Pidal; = hurtare, a tense now obsolete; modern hurtar)
fallaro: fallar — (if) I find (future subjunctive 1st sg., with the old -o ending, restored by Pidal as fallar[o]; menos le fallar[o] 'if I find him missing'; Pidal 'si le hallare menos, si le echare de menos'; = hallare, a tense now obsolete)
âquestos: a + aquestos — to these (a + demonstrative aquestos masc. pl.; â aquestos myos vassallos 'to these my vassals'; = a estos)
myos: mio — my (masc. pl.; myos vassallos 'my vassals'; = mis)
curian: curiar — they guard, watch over (present 3rd pl., paired with andan; curian a Valençia 'guard Valencia'; = guardan; no modern curiar)
arrobdando: arrobdar — making the rounds, patrolling (gerund; andan arrobdando 'go about on patrol'; Pidal: 'rondar, hacer el servicio de guardia exterior en una fortaleza'; = rondando)
corth: corth — court (= corte; so spelled, with final -th; no note in Pidal; here the Çid's court at Valencia)
falló: fallar — he found (preterite 3rd sg.; quando los falló 'when he had found them (all assembled)'; = halló)
fízolos: fazer + los — he made them (preterite 3rd sg. fizo + enclitic los; fízolos nonbrar 'had them named, called over'; = los hizo)
nonbrar: nonbrar — to name, call by name, call over (infinitive; = nombrar)
çientos: çiento — hundred (masc., pl. in compounds; seys çientos 'six hundred'; = cientos, modern seiscientos)
alégrasle: alegrar + se + le — it rejoices for him (present 3rd sg. alégra + reflexive s(e), written -s, + enclitic le dative; alégrasle el coraçón 'his heart rejoices'; = se le alegra)
sonrrisar: sonrrisar — to smile (infinitive; tornós a sonrrisar 'he began to smile'; = sonreír)
ixiemos: exir — we went out, left (preterite 1st pl., old -iemos ending; = salimos; no modern exir)
destas: de + estas — of these (preposition de + demonstrative estas fem. pl.; destas mis ganançias 'of these my gains'; = de estas)
ídgelos: id + ge + los — go … them to him (imperative 2nd pl. of ir, id, + ge, old dative 'to him', ancestor of modern se, + los 'them'; e vos ídgelos levar 'and do you go and take them to him'; = id a llevárselos)
besalde: besar + le — kiss … his (imperative 2nd pl. besad + enclitic le, with -dl- > -ld-; besalde la mano 'kiss his hand'; = besadle)
rogad: rogar — ask, beg (imperative 2nd pl.; firme gelo rogad 'ask it of him earnestly'; = rogad)
naturales: natural — natural, by blood, true-born (adjective, pl.; mis fijas naturales 'my daughters by birth'; = naturales; Pidal's bracketed supplied word)
quenlas: que + me + las — that … me … them (Pidal's note to v. 1277: quenlas dexe 'que me las deje', 'that he let me have them'; the me worn down to its consonant, written n before l, cf. quem; = que me las)
dexe: dexar — (that) he let, allow (present subjunctive 3rd sg.; quenlas dexe sacar 'that he let me take them out'; = deje)
sacar: sacar — to take out, bring away (infinitive; dexe sacar 'let (me) take (them) out'; = sacar)
enbiaré: enbiar — I shall send (future 1st sg.; enbiaré por ellas 'I shall send for them'; = enviaré)
sabed: saber — know, take note of (imperative 2nd pl.; e vos sabed el mensage 'and you, learn the message'; = sabed)
vernán: venir — they will come (future 3rd pl., syncopated, with n and r changing places: venir-án > vernán; = vendrán)
ciento: ciento — hundred (full form before a noun; ciento omnes 'a hundred men'; = cien, ciento)
servirle: servir + le — to serve him (infinitive + enclitic le; por servirle 'to serve him'; = servirle)
carrera: carrera — road, way, journey (en la carrera 'on the road'; = carrera, now mostly 'race, career')

__broaden__.armas: arma — weapon, arms (pl.; armas de lidiar 'weapons for fighting'; en armas 'in arms, armed'; = armas) · also armas — men-at-arms, armed men (treynta mill de armas 'thirty thousand armed men')
__broaden__.parte: parte — part, side (de parte de los moros 'on the Moors' side'; = parte) · also partir (se) — he parts, leaves (present 3rd sg. of partir, with non se le: que nos le parte de so braço 'who does not leave his side'; = se aparta)
__broaden__.ivan: ir — they were going (imperfect 3rd pl.; ivan posar 'they were going to lodge'; = iban) · also ir + gerund, 'were coming to, gradually' (ya lo ivan provando 'they were by now coming to experience it')
__broaden__.vale: valer — it is worth (present 3rd sg.; que más vale de mill marcos 'which is worth more than a thousand marks'; = vale) · also va + le — 'it goes on (…ing) for him' (ir + gerund with enclitic le: Yal creçe la barba e vale allongando 'and it goes on lengthening for him'; = se le va alargando)
__broaden__.passar: passar — to cross, pass over (infinitive; = pasar) · also passar — 'to pass through, pierce' (tanta adágara foradar e passar 'so many shields pierced and passed through') · also noun el passar 'the crossing' (en el passar de Xúcar 'at the crossing of the Júcar'; = el paso)
__broaden__.fo: seer (and ir, which shares this preterite) — he/it was; went (preterite 3rd sg.; = fue, restored by Pidal as f[o]; of this part's three occurrences, fo entrado and fo acusado are periphrastic/passive ser + past part. constructions, while fo algo is a plain copula with a pronoun predicate, 'was something') · also commo fo tu voluntad, ca fo tu voluntad 'as/for it was your will' (ser + noun subject, 'it was'; Pidal restores f[o]) · also se fo acomendar 'went to commend himself' (ir); fo de noch 'it was night' (ser de + noun, 'night had come'); fo desenparada (passive, 'was abandoned') · also fo — went (ir; mañanas fo Minaya 'in the morning Minaya went'); fo de moros 'it came from the Moors' (ser de + noun of origin; Pidal restores f[o]) · also fo — it was, ser + adjective predicate (Buena fo la de Valençia 'good was the (capture) of Valencia'; Pidal restores f[o])
__broaden__.pocos: poco — few (masc. pl.) · also más pocos 'fewer' (Con más pocos ixiemos 'with fewer we went out'; Pidal 'menos', cf. más mucho)
__broaden__.mucho: mucho — much, greatly · also mucho — very, intensifying a predicate (mucho es mañana 'it is much too early, too soon') · also mas mucho — 'more' (mucho as a comparative = más: mas mucho fue provechosa 'was more profitable'; Pidal)
__broaden__.arrancada: arrancada — rout, headlong flight; also the pursuit and rout of the enemy (de arrancada 'in rout'; el arrancada, el before a vowel-initial fem. noun; = arrancada) · also 'victory' (Pidal's gloss at v. 1233: esta arrancada 'this victory')
__broaden__.nuevas: nueva — news, tidings (fem. pl.; sus nuevas legavan 'his news was arriving'; = noticias, nuevas) · also nuevas — renown, fame (las nuevas de mio Çid sonando van; Pidal 'renombre, fama') · also nuevas — affairs, doings (las nuevas del cavallero 'the knight's affairs'; Pidal 'los asuntos, los negocios')
__broaden__.guisa: guisa — manner, fashion; a guisa de 'in the fashion of' · a vuestra guisa 'as you see fit, in your own way' (prended a vuestra guisa 'take as you please') · also de guisa que 'in such a way that' (de guisa irán por ellas que … 'in such a manner will they go for them that …'; = de modo que)
__broaden__.voluntad: voluntad — will, willingness; de voluntad e de grado, a doubled formula, 'willingly and gladly' · God's will (commo fo tu voluntad 'as was your will'); de toda voluntad 'with all one's heart' · also de buena voluntad 'gladly, willingly' (the formula of assent); a toda su voluntad 'wholly to his satisfaction, at his will'
__broaden__.le: le — to him, him (dative pronoun) · also le — him, as direct object (leísmo; si ellos le prenden 'if they take him'); dative (non se le dava 'did not surrender to him') · also le — dative of separation, 'from him' (que nos le parte de so braço 'who does not leave his side'); dative 'for him' (ques le non spidiés 'who does not take leave of him')
__broaden__.por: por — through, along, by, for · purpose, 'in order to' (por el reyno quitar 'to quit the kingdom'); por + inf. 'yet to be done' (tres an por troçir 'three remain to pass'); 'for, on behalf of' (por mio Çid) · also por — 'out of, because of' (por miedo 'through fear'); 'for (that reason)' (por tal lo faze 'he does it for that reason'); 'by way of' (por Guadalfajara); por + noun 'for the sake of' ; por coraçón 'willingly' · also 'for (a price)' (por quanto serié conprada 'for how much it would be bought'); 'by means of' (por carta 'by writ'); 'through, thanks to' (por mí ganaredes 'through me you will gain') · also por — 'on, during (a time)' (por aquesta mañana 'this morning'); 'by way of, through' (por medio de la llaña 'through the middle of the plain') · also por — 'in' after fiar (yo fío por Dios 'I trust in God') · also por — 'to fetch, for' after enbiar/ir (enbiaré por ellas, irán por ellas 'I shall send for them', 'they will go for them'); por cuenta 'by count, in a count'
